title: Patch: the game log speaks its newest line to screen readers

**Issue #4140 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4140: Patch: the game log speaks its newest line to screen readers
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

A blind player hears the game as it happens. Today the turn banner announces whose turn it is and a failed attack explains itself, but the ordinary feed of the match, your opponent played a unit, your unit took damage, a trap fired, stays silent unless the reader leaves the board and finds the log. After this change a screen reader speaks each newest log line once, politely, as it lands, so a player who cannot see the board can follow the game hands-free. Sighted players see nothing different.

Concrete example: the opponent plays a unit. Today a screen-reader user hears nothing until the turn banner changes. After the change they hear the same sentence the log shows, e.g. the unit was played, once, without moving their focus.

## Why

- The log is the screen-reader player's window into the match (SPEC §10.10, R745), and its lines are already safe to speak: redacted cards are never named (R97), so an announcement leaks nothing the view hides (CLAUDE.md rule 7).
- The gap is concrete in code: `Log.tsx` renders `<ol aria-label="Game log">` with no live region, and a search of `Log.tsx`, `Game.tsx` and `Log.test.tsx` finds no `aria-live`, `role="status"` or visually-hidden announcer for log lines. The only spoken updates are the turn banner (`role="status"` in `Game.tsx`), attack-failure and error notes.
- Axe (e2e spec 38) passes on the board, but axe cannot require a live feed, so the gate stays green while the feed stays mute.
- Precedent exists for screen-reader-only presentation: a full-art face keeps its name in its words for a screen reader (R2723000). This extends that thinking to the log.
- None of the open issues covers it, and none of the rejected ones is the same idea: #1040 was scroll position, #1692 was a visual unread badge on the phone toggle, #431 was the broader board support this builds on.

## Proposal

- Add a visually-hidden announcer inside the log component: one element using the existing visually-hidden pattern (`board.css`, as the turn plate does), with `aria-live="polite"` and `aria-atomic="true"`, whose text is the plain words of the newest shown line.
- Announce only arrivals: the announcer updates when the newest line's key changes, never re-reads kept history on mount, on reveal of the phone popover, or on re-render, so opening the log does not replay up to 1000 lines.
- Announce the redacted-safe line text the log already draws (never an instance id), including the turn divider as the turn's own line where one exists.
- Rejected alternative: putting `aria-live` on the whole `<ol>` (screen readers would re-read history on every change) or using `assertive` (would interrupt the player's own navigation and the turn banner).

## Where it lands

- `apps/web/src/game/Log.tsx`: the announcer element beside the `<ol>`, fed by the same `shown` lines the list draws.
- `apps/web/src/game/board.css` (or the existing visually-hidden pattern it already holds): no new visual style, reuse the pattern.
- `apps/web/src/game/Log.test.tsx`: new tests for the announcer.
- SPEC §10.10 (`spec/10-engine-guide.md`, Client rendering, R745): cite as the grounding section; no spec wording or ruling change needed (presentation only, no Hearthstone decision, so no new ruling note).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With a screen reader, the newest log line is announced once when it lands (new event window), and opening or re-rendering the board announces nothing extra.
- [ ] A redacted line announces exactly its shown redacted words (no hidden card name, no instance id), per R97.
- [ ] No visual change: board screenshots and pixel specs are untouched; the announcer takes no layout space.
- [ ] New unit tests in `Log.test.tsx` fail without the change and pass with it (arrival announces; mount/reveal does not replay history; redacted stays redacted).
- [ ] The existing accessibility gate (e2e spec 38) still passes with no new axe exception.

## Size and risks

Small: one element plus Vergil-style key-change gating and unit tests, roughly one file changed and one test file extended. Main risk is verbosity taste (which lines deserve speech, e.g. every damage tick vs. turn boundaries); the safe default is every newest line, matching the visible log, tunable later from player feedback. No hidden-information risk: the announcer reads only the already-redacted line text. No secret, dashboard, or account work.
```
